ir.name: weighted_advantage_exp_margin_logsigmoid_tanh_scaled_weighted_mean
ir.intuition: To reduce the similarity to the previous linear exponential margin methods, I introduced a tanh nonlinearity to smoothly scale the margin, making it a bounded adaptive margin rather than unbounded exponential. Additionally, I scaled the normalized advantage gap by the tanh-transformed mean advantage ensuring the margin is both normalized and smoothly adjusted. This change preserves dynamic margin adaptation while significantly differentiating the nonlinearity shape and scaling, improving novelty and stability.
ir.pseudocode:
epsilon=1e-6
mean_adv = mean(advantage_gap)
margin = tanh(clamp(abs(mean_adv), 0, 1))
norm = max(mean(norm(advantage_gap)), epsilon)
x_raw = (log_prob_w - log_prob_l) / norm
x = margin * x_raw
x = clamp(x, -20, 20)
loss = -logsigmoid(x)
loss_weighted = loss * weight
return sum(loss_weighted) / max(sum(weight), epsilon)
ir.code:
def generated_loss(batch, model_output, extra):
    lpw = batch['log_prob_w']
    lpl = batch['log_prob_l']
    weight = batch['weight']
    advantage_gap = batch['advantage_gap']
    epsilon = 1e-6
    mean_adv = ops.mean(advantage_gap)
    abs_mean_adv = ops.abs(mean_adv)
    clamped_mean_adv = ops.clamp(abs_mean_adv, 0.0, 1.0)
    margin = ops.tanh(clamped_mean_adv)
    norm_per_sample = ops.norm(advantage_gap)
    norm = ops.maximum(ops.mean(norm_per_sample), epsilon)
    x_raw = ops.div(ops.sub(lpw, lpl), norm)
    x = ops.mul(margin, x_raw)
    x = ops.clamp(x, -20.0, 20.0)
    loss = ops.neg(ops.logsigmoid(x))
    loss_weighted = ops.mul(loss, weight)
    loss_mean = ops.div(ops.sum(loss_weighted), ops.maximum(ops.sum(weight), epsilon))
    return loss_mean
